questions.q: How does the lesson distinguish Trailhead from the Trailblazer Community?
options: They are the same product with two different names
The Trailblazer Community is only for certified Architects
Trailhead is for networking, and the Trailblazer Community is for coursework
Trailhead is the learning platform; the Trailblazer Community is the people layer built around it
questions.explain: The lesson draws a clear line: Trailhead is the learning platform, and the Trailblazer Community is the real, active people layer around it.

questions.q: Which four places does the lesson name as the real, concrete parts of the Trailblazer Community?
options: Feed, Groups, Topics, and Group Meetings
Badges, Points, Ranks, and Superbadges
Resumes, Portfolios, GitHub, and LinkedIn
Administrator, Developer, Consultant, and Architect
questions.explain: The lesson names Feed, Groups, Topics, and Group Meetings as the concrete places where community participation happens.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say an answer posted on the Feed is a more checkable signal than a badge count alone?
options: Because Feed answers are anonymous and can't be traced to anyone
Because Feed answers automatically count as certifications
Because it's tied to your real, public Trailhead profile, making it a visible, attributable example of your judgment
Because badges are always fake and Feed answers are always real
questions.explain: The lesson explains that Feed answers are visible and attributable, tied to the same public profile set up in Lesson 3.

questions.q: What does the lesson say makes a local Trailblazer Community Group meeting valuable for a job search?
options: It guarantees a job offer within 30 days
It's a room full of people who already work in Salesforce, in your market, sometimes including the people doing the hiring
It replaces the need for a resume entirely
It is only open to certified Technical Architects
questions.explain: The lesson describes local group meetings as real rooms of working Salesforce professionals, sometimes including people doing the hiring.

questions.q: What sustainable starting cadence does the lesson suggest for answering questions on the Feed?
options: Every single day, regardless of topic
Once per year, right before a job search begins
Only after becoming a certified Technical Architect
One real question every week or two, in an area close to your actual capstone work
questions.explain: The lesson suggests answering one real question every week or two as a realistic, sustainable starting cadence.
